claim: NJSBDC at Rutgers-New Brunswick resource entry: cost is 'No-cost (published as "NO-COST, 1-on-1 consultation")'
problem: The quoted phrase does not appear on the cited page (https://njsbdc.com/njsbdc-at-rutgers-university-new-brunswick/), which only describes training/counselling, the virtual-only Middlesex office, phone/email and Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30 hours. No cost statement is on that page at all, so the quotation is unsupported as written. The substance (little or no cost) is real but lives on a different page.
fix: Drop the quotation mark phrasing and cite https://njsbdc.com/about-us/, which states services are provided 'at no cost'; or quote the Rutgers page's actual wording on virtual service delivery only.

claim: Stripe/Tidemark benchmark finding: 'median net revenue retention was 110% for multi-product companies versus single-product firms hovering around 100%'
problem: The chart on the cited page gives median NRR of 110% for multi-product and 105% for single-product, not ~100%. The report's prose does say single-product firms 'hover around 100% or slightly below unless they raise prices', so the brief reflects the narrative but contradicts the printed median by 5 points.
fix: State the printed medians: 110% multi-product vs 105% single-product, and note the report's comment that single-product NRR clusters near or below 100% absent price rises.

claim: Recommendation 2: price the pilot 'near the low end of the published range (roughly $3,000-$7,500)'
problem: No source in the brief publishes a $3,000 pilot price. The only published numbers in the brief are Skcript's USD 7,500 pilot and 'from USD 4,000' check-up, so the stated low end of the 'published range' is invented, even though the recommendation is labelled as inference.
fix: Either describe the range as the consultant's own judgment (with no 'published range' framing) or use the actually published $4,000-$7,500 band.

claim: ScalePad 2026 MSP Trends Report finding rated strength 'High'
problem: Strength ratings are supposed to reflect sample size and relevance. The cited chapter page discloses no respondent count or methodology, so a 'High' rating rests on a sample the reader cannot inspect; it is also MSP data used as an analogue for AI consultancies.
fix: Downgrade to Medium unless a stated sample size can be cited, and note the MSP-to-AI-consultancy gap in the finding itself.

problem: The pricing page is undated, so the 2026 year label is an assumption rather than something the source states. It is used only as a structural example, so the risk is low, but the year should not be presented as sourced.
